newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends higher, session uneventful.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends higher, session uneventful.

text.p: CSCE world sugar ended modestly higher in quiet trading Monday, bolstered by steady buying from both speculators and the trade, dealers said.

After surviving an early-session test of key chart support levels, prices sprang back into positive territory and remained there for the rest of the day. Good trade buying of October and on the nearby October-March switch was noted, as well as commission-house interest in the deferreds.

Views that the market was substantially oversold contributed to today's gains, dealers said. Most-active March futures have fallen by about half a cent since hitting contract highs at the beginning of the month.
"The trade was the better buyer today," said one. "They are taking the opportunity to get some very good prices compared with where we were a week ago."
March rose 0.06 cent per lb, to 11.27, having traded from 11.17 to 11.28. Spot October gained 0.11, to 11.30, retaking its premium to the deferreds.
With many market operators away for the Yom Kippur holiday, the session was more subdued than usual, traders said. But overall turnover reached a fairly sizable 18,518 lots by the close.

Speculators for their part were still assumed to have a fairly significant position in spot October, which has six trading days to go before its expiry. Total open interest on the contract totalled 26,047 lots as of last Friday's close. With so many uncovered positions, the nearby switch would likely remain volatile through the week's end.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
